title: Hacking with Claude on a $27 Smart Watch: Building a Custom Watch Face Using AI
summary: The author details their experience using AI coding assistants (primarily open-weight models like Kimi and DeepSeek) to develop a custom watch face for the PineTime, a $27 open-source smartwatch. The project leverages the watch's open-source firmware (InfiniTime), well-documented ecosystem, and simulator (InfiniSim) to create a functional prototype with AI guidance. The post highlights the iterative process, challenges (e.g., performance limitations, text positioning), and solutions (e.g., using a fullscreen background image for static elements). The author shares their code and lessons learned on GitHub for others to replicate or build upon.
key_points: The PineTime is a $27 open-source smartwatch with customizable firmware (InfiniTime) and a simulator (InfiniSim) for development.
AI coding assistants (e.g., Claude, Kimi, DeepSeek) can accelerate firmware development by generating code, orchestrating tasks, and iterating on feedback.
The project started with replicating a Casio-style watch face from a reference image, using an existing InfiniTime watch face as a template.
Initial AI-generated code required manual refinement due to inaccuracies in text sizing and positioning, but provided a usable starting point.
A hybrid approach was used: static elements were rendered as a fullscreen background image, while dynamic elements (e.g., time) were programmed separately to optimize performance.
Performance limitations were encountered on the physical device (e.g., slow Bluetooth transfers, delayed screen refreshes), but the prototype remained functional.
The author emphasizes the value of AI in low-stakes, exploratory projects, enabling rapid iteration and reducing barriers to entry for firmware development.
All code and documentation (including an AGENTS.md guide) are shared on GitHub for community reuse.
